premises: Sub-nanometric CoNiCuZnPd HEA clusters on CeO2 nanorods exhibit structural reversibility under oxidative/reductive cycling.
This reversibility involves sacrificial oxidation of non-noble metals forming oxide shells around noble metal cores.
The oxide shells sterically hinder noble metal interactions and inhibit diffusion into the support.
Hydrogen spillover on CeO2 (110) facets aids the formation of these HEA clusters.
Limiting oxygen spillover will prevent the formation of transient oxides, causing irreversible segregation and sintering.
